en: The Sūtra on the Dissolution of the Summer Retreat,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmabhadra, Imperially Appointed Dazhoucheng Fudao,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Great Master Mingjiao, under Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove Monastery in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a community of five hundred bhikṣus. All were arhats whose taints were exhausted, who had accomplished what was to be done, laid down their heavy burdens, attained their own benefit, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose minds were well-liberated.

There was only one bhikṣu currently abiding in the stage of training (śaikṣa), for whom the Blessed One had already given a prophecy, saying that he would see the Dharma, attain the Dharma, and realize the fruit of perfection.

At that time, when the Blessed One’s summer retreat (varṣā) had concluded and it was time to break the retreat, on the fifteenth day, he arranged his seat together with the assembly of bhikṣus and sat down.
When the assembly had taken their seats, the Buddha addressed the community of bhikṣus, saying:
"I have now attained the tranquility of the holy life (brahmacarya); this is my final body, for by means of the unsurpassed medicine, I have eradicated all ailments."
"My disciples have fully understood and thoroughly mastered all phenomena; therefore, I shall now declare the rules for the conclusion of the summer retreat (varṣā).
O assembly of bhikṣus!
Regarding all my physical, verbal, and mental actions during this summer retreat, may you grant me your forbearance?"

At that time, having heard the Buddha’s words, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"As the Buddha has taught, we have now attained the tranquility of the holy life (*brahmacarya*) up to the point where our bodily, verbal, and mental actions are patient.
We know that the Buddha’s bodily, verbal, and mental actions are free from all faults; therefore, we monks have nothing further to be patient with."

What do you think? Our Buddha, the World-Honored One, is able to tame those who are difficult to tame; he is skilled at bringing rest to those who have no rest; he is skilled at comforting those who lack peace; and he causes those who are not yet tranquil to attain tranquility. The Tathāgata has thoroughly realized the right path, well-expounded the right path, and revealed the right path. Even for us who delight in the enlightenment of the śrāvakas, the Buddha has well-expounded it, causing the śrāvakas and others to practice according to principle and realize the fruit of sainthood.
"Therefore, we cannot endure the conduct of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, regarding his body, speech, and mind.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I now, before the Buddha, seek the Buddha’s forbearance for all unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"I shall grant my forbearance regarding all the actions of body, speech, and mind that you currently possess."
What do you think, Śāriputra? You are endowed with ethical discipline and extensive learning;

you have few desires and are content; you have severed all afflictions and exerted great diligence; you dwell securely in right mindfulness and possess the wisdom of meditative equipoise, the wisdom of hearing, quick-witted wisdom, sharp wisdom, the wisdom of renunciation, the wisdom of thorough penetration, vast and pure wisdom, profound wisdom, and incomparable wisdom—you are possessed of the jewel of great wisdom.

He causes those who have not seen [the truth] to see; he brings those who are not yet disciplined to discipline; he expounds the Dharma for those who have not heard it; and he causes those possessed of anger to rejoice. He is able to preach the Dharma to the fourfold assembly without weariness.
Just as a prince of the golden wheel receives consecration and succeeds to the royal throne, governing according to the Dharma;
so too are you, Śāriputra!

You are my son, having received the dharma of consecration and succeeded to the position of the Dharma King. Just as I have turned the unsurpassed wheel of the Dharma, so have you, like me, realized the exhaustion of outflows and attained liberation.
"Therefore, Śāriputra, I now approve of all your three types of karma.
When Śāriputra heard that the Buddha had approved, he prostrated himself in sincere gratitude.
Again he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

Just as the Buddha has granted his acceptance of my three types of action, among those present in this assembly there are five hundred bhikṣus whose bodily, verbal, and mental actions have been unwholesome; I only pray that the World-Honored One will likewise grant his acceptance."
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"I can also tolerate the three types of karma of these five hundred bhikṣus.
What do you think?"

These five hundred bhikṣus are all arhats; their taints are exhausted, they have accomplished what was to be done, laid down the heavy burden, attained their own benefit, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and their minds are well-liberated. There is only one bhikṣu who currently dwells in the stage of training, yet I have already bestowed a prediction upon this bhikṣu: having seen the Dharma and attained the Dharma, he shall realize the fruit of perfection.
“Śāriputra! For this reason, I can endure all three types of karma performed by these five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The three types of karma belonging to myself and this assembly of five hundred bhikṣus have already been forgiven by the Buddha.
I now have a doubt and shall again submit a request.”
May the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
explain this for me!
World-Honored One!
Among these five hundred bhikṣus, how many have attained the dharma of the three knowledges?
Furthermore, how many have attained both-fold liberation?
And how many have attained wisdom-liberation?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"Among these five hundred bhikṣus, ninety bhikṣus have attained the dharma of the three knowledges, ninety bhikṣus have attained both-fold liberation, and the remaining bhikṣus have attained wisdom-liberation."
“Śāriputra! Such bhikṣus have exhausted all afflictions and all abide in reality.
At that time, there was a venerable one in the assembly named Vāgīśa, who had this thought:
"I shall now, before the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, offer praise by reciting verses on the conclusion of the summer retreat.
Having formed this thought, the Venerable Vāgīśa rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverent devotion, spoke these verses:
"On the fifteenth day of the summer retreat’s end, Pure in conduct and observant of the Vinaya..."
The assembly of five hundred bhikṣus has completely severed the bonds of affliction;
having exhausted all outflows (āsrava), they have realized the stage of the noble fruit.
With inner tranquility and outer discipline, they are liberated and free from existence.
Having reached the very limit of birth and death, all that was to be done has been accomplished;
the fetters of ignorance and self-conceit have been severed completely, leaving nothing behind.
My Buddha, the Most Honored One, has eradicated all dharmas of false thought.
Having severed all tainted phenomena (*sāsrava-dharma*), he has skillfully removed the suffering of the disease of craving.
When craving is extinguished, it does not arise again; having left behind grasping like a great lion, he has exhausted all fears of existence. He alone is the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
Just as a Golden Wheel-Turning King is constantly surrounded by a thousand sons,
skillfully governing the four continents and subduing the borders of the four seas;
or like one who has achieved victory in battle, he is the supreme tamer of men.
The Śrāvakas attain the three knowledges, And likewise transcend the law of death.
All sons of the Buddha are thus: Realizing cessation, they are not born again.
I now pay homage to the Dharma King, To the unsurpassed Vairocana.
When the bhikṣu Vāgīśa had spoken these verses, he returned to his original seat.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra and the other bhikṣus, having heard the Buddha proclaim the rules for the end of the summer retreat (*varṣā*), felt their minds become keen and clear; they leaped with joy and, with faith, accepted and practiced them.
The Sūtra on the Resolution of the Summer Retreat Spoken by the Buddha.
